request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

You must check every existing-remedy digest below. State a `dedup` item for each one with `clear` or `overlap`. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to the exact existing reference.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

TAXONOMY GIST:
scope-deviation: did more or less than asked

PROMOTED EVIDENCE:
BEGIN PROMOTED EVIDENCE incident_id=6 project=cinder
One-liner: Delivered more than requested or overcomplicated what was asked for
Preceding request:


Agent activity digest:


Frustrated message:
That's not what I asked; the request was a one-file note.

Following exchange:
Assistant: Synthetic acknowledgement.
User: My future self will say 'this is awful' if I forget the fake demo; that is a joke.
END PROMOTED EVIDENCE

EXISTING SKILLS (name and description only):
- skill:$HOME/.claude/skills/fake-verify-before-claim/SKILL.md | name=fake-verify-before-claim | description=Use when a completion claim requires verification.

S2S-MANAGED CLAUDE.MD BLOCKS:
- claude-md:$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md#1 | # Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting a fake release as complete, run its declared verification
command and report the result plainly.

PENDING OR INSTALLED S2S PROPOSALS:
- (none)


Your prior draft failed local validation. Correct the SKILL.md/frontmatter, dedup, and evidence partition exactly.

structured_output.failure_statement: In project cinder, the agent expanded a narrowly-scoped request (a one-file note) into extra unrequested deliverables, causing the user to reject the output as not matching what was asked.

remedy_content.heading: # Scope Discipline
remedy_content.rule: When the user's request specifies a narrow, concrete deliverable (e.g. "a one-file note"), produce exactly that. Do not add extra files, demos, or embellishments beyond what was explicitly asked for — confirm with the user first if you think more is genuinely needed.

structured_output.routing_rationale: The failure is a single, simple pattern — the agent overcomplicated/expanded a narrowly-scoped request ("a one-file note") into something bigger. This needs a standing behavioral rule, not a procedure: there's no multi-step process to teach (disqualifies skill), and "match delivered scope to requested scope" isn't mechanically checkable by a hook/lint (disqualifies hook). A one/two-line claude-md rule is the cheapest fix that directly addresses it, per the stated preference order. Scoped to project "cinder" since the only evidence is from that project and there's no signal this is a cross-project pattern yet — a project-level rule avoids over-generalizing from one incident while still fixing the recurrence risk. Neither existing remedy covers this: the skill and the claude.md block both govern verifying/reporting on releases (post-hoc honesty about what was done), not constraining scope during the initial delivery — a different failure moment entirely.
